title: Windable knots count approximately
claim: Every knot is strictly terraced in McQuillan's sense because of K2 (no two excluded tuples adjacent). A knot is windable exactly when it excludes at most two tuples or is a parity knot (26 of 34), decided both by McQuillan's three-place inequality and by exact feasibility of his definition; the 8 knots excluding three tuples (a parity class minus one) are not windable. Given McQuillan's winding theorem, native counting with pins and free legs has a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for every windable knot; with exact formulas for the four topological knots, only the six non-symmetric knots excluding three tuples lack an efficient counting algorithm.
failure_conditions: A knot that is not strictly terraced.
A windability verdict that differs from the census, or a non-windable knot that does not exclude three tuples.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite census of three-place relations; the approximation algorithms are cited external theorems. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, exact simplex over fractions) confirms the terraced property, the census by two independent tests, and four controls reproducing published verdicts. The approximation scheme is a cited external theorem. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exact finite checks; conditional algorithmic corollary
